title: Evidence and Sources
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of claim support and citation evaluation
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: Whether the cited passage supports the specific claim
Whether a source reference resolves to the intended record

blocks.text: An answer has four factual claims. Three have citations, but only two are supported by their cited passages. All links exist.
Claim support is 2/4=50%; citation presence is 3/4=75%; link existence among three citations is 3/3. These measure different failures.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: An answer has four factual claims. Three have citations, but only two are supported by their cited passages. All links exist. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Claim support is 2/4=50%; citation presence is 3/4=75%; link existence among three citations is 3/3. These measure different failures.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Five claims; four cited; three supported by cited passages; one cited ID is nonexistent. Compute support and citation presence and explain link limits.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Support=3/5=60%; citation presence=4/5=80%. Link checks reject the nonexistent ID; remaining real links still need entailment checks.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Citation counts do not establish truth beyond the supplied sources or the correctness of uncited claims.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: A closer explanation
For this classroom rubric count a claim as supported only when its cited passage entails it. Separately count correct citation links. Use the number of factual claims as the support denominator.
